topics.topic: Send-time manifest/header revalidation scope and which failures map to binding_stale vs operation_failed
questions: Exactly which rule-5 checks are re-evaluated before send as "record itself" (and therefore produce `binding_stale`) versus excluded from that set?

If manifest instance headers change later (without capability digest change) to include a forbidden kernel-set header name (e.g. `accept-encoding`, `content-type`) but not as a duplicate, which exact pre-send failure detail must be produced?
At send time, exactly which manifest/header failures must conclude `binding_stale` versus `operation_failed` instance details such as `required_header_repeated`?

quotes: When the record cannot be read or fails one of rule 5's checks of the record itself — not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own — the entry is absent, the operation is no longer invocable, or its digest differs from the binding's pin, nothing is sent and the element concludes `operation_failed` with detail `binding_stale` (A09 rule 6).

or names one required header twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`;

At send time the instance checks are A09 rule 6's, with their own details (`instance_not_selected`, `instance_address_missing` — the same "counts as none" as A08 rule 5 —, `required_header_repeated`, `plain_http_not_allowed`); only the checks of the record itself give `binding_stale` (A08 rule 6).
judgement.why: The rules explicitly split record-self failures from instance failures and name the corresponding failure details.
